extracted.intended_audience: college/university instructors and educators implementing peer-review writing assignments (especially in science/neuroscience courses)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and running Calibrated Peer Review (CPR) assignments in undergraduate courses: creating prompts and calibration essays, training students in calibration, administering anonymous multi-rater peer review, and scoring essays using CPR's automated and instructor-mediated controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear grading parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: CPR is designed to minimize problems with peer assessment through the use of clear criteria of grading parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructors set explicit evaluation parameters (e.g., ten style and content questions) so reviewers judge against well-defined standards; ambiguity in criteria leads to student confusion, so spend time clarifying questions and acceptable answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized 'calibrating' practice session
rubrics_metrics.description: A standardized ‘calibrating’ practice session in peer review is required prior to evaluating peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students evaluate three instructor-provided calibration essays and learn how their evaluations compare to the instructor’s; failing calibration can be remediated with a second attempt and instructor comments, which serves as training and quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double anonymity of reviewers and reviewees
rubrics_metrics.description: CPR implements double anonymity (anonymous reviewers and anonymous reviewees) and random distribution of peer essays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-blind distribution simplifies organization and helps guarantee anonymity, reducing some forms of bias but it may increase student perception of 'subjective' grading due to lack of context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multiple reviewers of each essay
rubrics_metrics.description: Each essay should be reviewed by multiple anonymous peers (in this implementation, three anonymous peer reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple reviews increase reliability; CPR generates a mean text rating from the weighted average of peer reviews and flags essays reviewed by too few peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose high-, mid-, and low-quality calibration essays
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructors must compose high, low, and mid-quality calibration essays for the calibration stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibration essays exemplify different quality levels and are used to train students on the rubric; include instructor evaluations of these essays for comparison and feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use focused content and style evaluation questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation parameters comprise content (1–8) and style (9–10) questions addressing global, paragraph, and sentence levels, answerable in yes/no or none/one/some formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These questions operationalize the rubric across levels (main idea, organization, transitions, word choice, grammar); ensure questions are interpretable—rigid yes/no formats can cause confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a holistic text rating (1–10)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to itemized content/style questions, students give a holistic text rating for each essay on a 1–10 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holistic ratings are changeable per assignment and used in conjunction with acceptable deviation ranges to assess review accuracy; they form the primary numeric measure of essay quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set acceptable deviation ranges and question-passing thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructors set the grading criteria for calibrations: the number of specific questions a student must answer correctly and the acceptable deviation range for holistic evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These thresholds determine whether a student 'passes' calibration and therefore whether their peer-review contributions will count; choose ranges that balance strictness and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require calibration accuracy for peer-review credit
rubrics_metrics.description: If a student does not 'pass' calibration evaluations, their peer reviews do not factor into the calculation of text ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides quality control by excluding unreliable reviewers; offer remediation so students can improve and participate fully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score assignments using combined components (essay + review accuracies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final scores combine essay quality and the accuracy of calibration reviews, peer reviews, and self review as determined by the instructor's weighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example weighting used: text 15% (5% per essay), accuracy of three peer reviews 60%, accuracy of calibration reviews 15% (5% each), and self review accuracy 10%; instructors may set different weights depending on pedagogical goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine review accuracy by correlation with peers/instructor
rubrics_metrics.description: The accuracy of reviews is determined by correlation with other students’ evaluations (and instructor calibrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statistical congruence to measure reviewer reliability rather than solely subjective judgment; explain to students how accuracy is computed to avoid confusion or strategic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use automated scoring flags for anomalies
rubrics_metrics.description: A scoring algorithm flags the instructor to potential errors in analysis (e.g., essays reviewed by fewer than three peers, peer reviews with significant variance, or essays reviewed by poorly calibrated students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated flags guide instructor review and regrading decisions; instructors should inspect flagged cases and have authority to adjust scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide mandatory tutorial/training on the CPR interface
rubrics_metrics.description: Before assignments, students complete a mandatory, online interactive tutorial on using the CPR interface and stages of the assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tutorials reduce technical confusion and familiarize students with composing, calibrating, and reviewing; minimal technical complaints were reported after one assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer instructor feedback and opportunities to revise calibration judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: After initial calibration attempts, students receive instructor feedback (including extensive comments) and may revise their assessments before official scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second-chance calibration with explanatory comments clarifies judgment criteria and improves student alignment with instructor standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a self-review phase after peer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Students evaluate their own essays after reading a set number of peer essays (six in this implementation), and self-review accuracy is part of scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-review tends to be higher than peer ratings; include self-review accuracy as a separate component and discuss self-assessment biases with students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide immediate and detailed feedback to students
rubrics_metrics.description: Students can access peers’ narrative comments and comprehensive scores immediately after deadline completion; CPR provided three detailed peer assessments within five minutes in this study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely, detailed feedback supports learning and allows instructors to address misconceptions promptly; emphasize constructive narrative feedback, not just numeric scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain instructor oversight and ability to edit scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructors have access to all student work (texts, calibration and peer reviews), know who reviewed each essay, can change essay scores, edit assignment grades, and add commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor mediation is essential: re-evaluate automated scores, resolve disputes, and optionally show rationale to reviewers or only to authors to preserve learning integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor qualitative quality of reviews into participation/grading
rubrics_metrics.description: CPR grades peer review accuracy quantitatively but does not directly grade qualitative content of written feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To discourage sloppy or cruel comments that nonetheless score as accurate, instructors should incorporate the quality of written peer comments into participation grades or other grade components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide opportunities for essay revision
rubrics_metrics.description: CPR lacks a built-in revision process; instructors should create opportunities for revision (e.g., extra credit revisions) to support learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering revision improves student learning and permits instructor-student conversations about which peer suggestions to adopt; example policy: up to 40% of difference between grade and perfect score available for revision credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and mitigate gaming and perception of subjectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Students may attempt 'grade scheming' (e.g., rating a very good essay as an 8 to maximize acceptable deviation) and may perceive peer grading as subjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about acceptable deviation rules, discuss integrity, consider altering scoring rules to reduce incentives for gaming, and provide class calibration exercises to align judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design assignments with explicit goals, guiding questions, and source materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructors author assignments by providing goals, guiding questions, essay word length, and links to relevant source materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CPR interface to set assignment goals and provide readings/lecture links; clear prompts reduce ambiguity and focus student writing and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use class time to collectively evaluate sample essays
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective in-class evaluation of a sample essay helps clarify evaluation parameters and aligns peer judgments with instructor expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer assessments most closely match instructor assessments when judgments are based on well-understood criteria; spend ~1.5 class periods introducing program and evaluating examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the CPR database for administrative benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: CPR stores results in a database accessible to instructors: text entries, reviews, and review histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saved reviews are useful for writing recommendation letters, calculating participation grades, and preventing lost work; maintain privacy and confidentiality practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan instructor time and resource investment
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing CPR requires instructor time for introducing the program, composing assignments and calibrations, and re-evaluating scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated time: 1.5 class periods for introduction, 8–10 hours to create assignments and calibration essays, and 4–8 hours to re-evaluate contested items; reuse library assignments or hire assistants to reduce load.
